gen-gf-oxanium-gf-epunda-sans: Rope-like consistency runs through every stem and tail of Oxanium. Epunda Sans has generously sized e and a counters and tightly trimmed sidebearings, so extended reading moves along smoothly without snagging.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-ramabhadra: Oxanium draws its arms and legs at constant width, with a high x-height that makes the lowercase look large. Ramabhadra keeps longer reading clean and unhurried with its prominent x-height.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-viga: Viga reads in smooth, shadow-free strokes, its capitals barely standing taller than the letters around them. Oxanium supplies the commanding heading above, and Viga stays out of its way.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-yantramanav: Oxanium has no hairlines, so its finest strokes match its stems. Yantramanav has spacious terminal gaps and lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals, so extended text feels modern and tidy.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-allerta: Paprika spaces its letters well apart, and its counters breathe like a hollow reed cut open. Allerta follows with wide, loose tracking and a prominent x-height, so extended reading stays unhurried.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-cal-sans: Expressive Paprika sprawls its letters out, while Cal Sans runs a single stroke width through the whole alphabet. Short ascenders and a generous x-height make extended reading feel approachable.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-genos: Paprika scatters its letters at a distance, with low stroke contrast and a commanding, expressive feel. Genos tucks in beside it with tightly pressed glyphs and mild contrast, so the two never clash.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-hammersmith-one: Loose and loud: Paprika scatters its letters wide and lets its counters breathe. And where Paprika commands attention, Hammersmith One simply keeps things clean with rounded, cord-like strokes and crossbars matching the stems.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-inder: Barely any height difference separates capitals from lowercase here, which keeps the body text clean and professional. Inder does that quietly, leaving Paprika to be the commanding, expressive one.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-jaldi: Paprika sets scattered, expressive letters whose lowercase fills out as boldly as capitals would. But Jaldi, brushed on with barely a gap between letters and a gaping c, keeps extended reading approachable.
